clue.text: Engineer denigrates me to generate debate

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rig up, so the letters that follow are rebuilt into a new order

parts.note: twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up an argument by belittling the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is an argument between opposing sides, which is a synonym-level match for a dispute or difference of opinion.

clue.text: Clamour multiple times to get kids' meal

parts.note: a din is a loud noise or clamour
the same noise again, made plural to show it happens many times

explanation.surface: Children make a racket over and over until they are fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Multiple times' asks for the clamour word again, this time in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Din-dins is nursery baby talk for dinner, so it is a meal as spoken to small children.

clue.text: Entrance to shopping arcade is narrow

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is where you go in, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of shopping
a shopping arcade is a mall

explanation.surface: The doorway into a shopping arcade is cramped.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and narrow are synonyms when describing limited width or scope, as in a small margin.

clue.text: At last Arsenal overwhelmed by accolades following shot on target

indicators.note: following places the combined piece after the next one in reading order

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a go

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed, so one piece is swallowed inside another

parts.note: accolades are honours or awards

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: the final letter of Arsenal

explanation.surface: A football report: Arsenal finally swamped by praise after a shot on target.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of Arsenal goes inside the honours word, and the whole follows the attempt word. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Goalwards means towards the goal, which is where a shot on target is heading.

clue.text: Style of uplifting new beer

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something up means reading it from the bottom upward

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A craft beer that cheers you up has a certain style.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair or dash, a synonym for style in the sense of stylish confidence.

clue.text: Agencies claiming compliance on insurance scheme

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one word grabs another inside itself

parts.note: the media are agencies of mass communication
C is the symbol for compliance in physics, the inverse of stiffness
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Bodies are claiming they comply with the rules of an insurance plan.
explanation.walkthrough: C for compliance is obscure: it is the physics symbol for how easily something bends.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicare is the US federal health insurance programme for older people, so it is a state scheme of cover.

clue.text: Spicy sausage from New Delhi used jalapeno alternative, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a spicy sausage from New Delhi swapped in for jalapenos.
explanation.definitionFit: Nduja is a soft, spreadable, very hot pork sausage from Calabria in southern Italy.

clue.text: The vacuous politician's overdue blueprint

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses everything between its outer letters

parts.note: the outside letters of The
an MP is a Member of Parliament; the 's is read as is
overdue means late

explanation.surface: An empty-headed politician's plan is long delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician's is read as 'the politician is', so the abbreviation runs straight on to the lateness word.
explanation.definitionFit: A template and a blueprint are both patterns or models from which copies are made.

clue.text: Bill's name instead of Rex turning up

indicators.note: instead of says one letter takes the place of another within the word

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement
N is the abbreviation for name
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A man called Bill has his name in place of Rex's when he arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like a reversal signal but is the definition: an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival or coming, so it is the act of something turning up.

clue.text: Former protectorate in Germany, as Alan Davies describes

indicators.note: to describe can mean to trace round, so these words enclose the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Germany, through as and Alan, to the start of Davies

explanation.surface: The comedian Alan Davies talks about a former colony while in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasaland was a British protectorate in Africa until 1964, when it became independent Malawi.

clue.text: Greatly affect writer in university department

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letter for the institution

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
a pen is something that writes
D is the abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: A writer joins a university department and causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend someone's life is to turn it upside down, an idiom for disrupting or greatly affecting it.

clue.text: Home rule beginning to suck for those on partner's side

parts.note: to be home is to be in
a law is a rule

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of suck

explanation.surface: Political self-government is starting to look bad for one faction.
explanation.walkthrough: Home rule reads like Irish self-government but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In-laws are relatives by marriage, the family on a spouse's side.

clue.text: Mess is eating place serving meat loaf

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: a scrape is a mess or predicament
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: An army mess hall where meat loaf is being served.
explanation.walkthrough: Mess, eating and serving all suggest a canteen; mess is in fact a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapple is a US dish of pork scraps and cornmeal set in a loaf, sliced and fried.

clue.text: Parody defunct right-wing party not starting to make comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the remaining letters run back the other way
not starting means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: Veritas was a short-lived UK right-wing party founded by Robert Kilroy-Silk in 2005

explanation.surface: Mocking a dead right-wing party that cannot get a comeback started.
explanation.walkthrough: Few solvers remember Veritas, a UK party of 2005; drop its V and read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody imitates something for comic effect, which is a kind of satire, ridicule through mockery.

clue.text: Terminal affected where public transport runs?

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bus or train terminal is disrupted along the route.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramline is the rail track along which trams, a form of public transport, run through streets.

clue.text: Folk work in wood hut, ultimately, next to defensive mound

indicators.note: next to puts one piece directly beside the other
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of hut
a rampart is a defensive earth bank around a fort

explanation.surface: Country people building in timber put a hut beside an earthwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramp art is a folk art style of carved, notched wooden objects, often made from cigar boxes.

clue.text: Required Ms Platell to reject a party that she supports

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it out, so a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Amanda Platell is a journalist and former Conservative press secretary
taken as written, then removed
Platell worked for the Conservatives, whose members are Tories

explanation.surface: A columnist is required to reject one party that she backs.
explanation.walkthrough: Amanda Platell is a British newspaper columnist who was press secretary to Tory leader William Hague. Tory is a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandatory means compulsory, so something mandatory is required by rule.

clue.text: Biographer's left to swap places with female for anti-abortionist

indicators.note: swapping places means two letters exchange positions within the word

parts.note: a profiler writes profiles, short biographies; the 's is read as has
L is the abbreviation for left
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A biographer writes about a campaigner against abortion.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters trade places inside the profile writer's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-lifer campaigns against abortion, calling the stance pro-life.

clue.text: On the contrary, I see Channel Island can provide refuge

indicators.note: the contrary is the opposite way round, so the first word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
ah is what you say when you see a point
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Someone contradicts a claim, then agrees a Channel Island could offer shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reads as a set phrase but is a word plus its turnaround signal. Sark is a small island off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's ark is a byword for a refuge, the vessel that sheltered Noah's family from the Flood.

clue.text: Cancel Britain's terminal European exit

indicators.note: terminal means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Britain
E is the abbreviation for European
a gate is a way out of an enclosure

explanation.surface: A comment on the final European exit of Britain being called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Brexit, but exit is simply a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to nullify it, so negate and cancel are synonyms.

clue.text: Old monk, drunk, means well in the end

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering and jumbled, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of well

explanation.surface: An elderly monk who has been drinking still means well, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Anselm was an eleventh-century Benedictine monk who became Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Wrongly label or title male

parts.note: Mister is a title before a man's name
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A form asks about mislabelling or the title of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To misterm something is to call it by the wrong name, giving it an incorrect label.

clue.text: Clue to go for driven type

definitions.meaning: read in reverse: golf is the radio code word for G, and a ball is round like O, so the answer clues the word go
something struck with a golfer's driver, and also the typewriter element that carried the type

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is reverse wordplay: the answer, read as wordplay, spells the two-letter word go. The second puns on drivers and IBM golfball typewriters.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf ball is what a golfer hits off the tee with a driver, and the IBM golfball was a spherical typing head.

clue.text: Note British never getting naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British
taken as written, then stripped

explanation.surface: A memo saying British people never go nude.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note equal to two semibreves, the longest in common use.

clue.text: Frolics in thorny shrubs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: playful skipping about, larks
second meaning: the prickly Mediterranean bushes whose flower buds are pickled

explanation.surface: Someone romps about among prickly bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Capers are high-spirited antics, and the caper plant is a spiny shrub grown for its edible buds.

clue.text: Be discriminatory, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: sexist means discriminating on grounds of sex

explanation.surface: An instruction to be prejudiced, though not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' looks like a mere verb in the surface but is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being or reality.

clue.text: Union preventing monarch leaving

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: to block is to prevent
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A trade union is trying to stop the king from abdicating.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries or parties acting together, a union for a common purpose.

clue.text: Cast of Educating Essex

indicators.note: of says the letters are taken from within the following words

parts.note: the letters span the end of Educating and the first letter of Essex

explanation.surface: Names the actors of a TV show about a school in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Essex was a British fly-on-the-wall TV documentary about a secondary school. Cast is not the actors but a tint.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a slight tint of colour, as in a bluish cast, which is exactly a tinge.

clue.text: Austrian pop star gets number of bird

parts.note: Falco was the Austrian singer of Rock Me Amadeus
nine is a number

explanation.surface: An Austrian singer is given a number about a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' suggests a song, but it is just a numeral word.
explanation.definitionFit: Falconine is the adjective relating to falcons, so it means of a particular bird of prey.

clue.text: Policemen regularly sit by with crimes unfolding — a method now adopted worldwide

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: unfolding opens things out of their original shape, rearranging the letters
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police officers stand by as crimes unfold, using a method adopted everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system of measurement, based on metres and kilograms, is used by nearly every country.
